Parse the output of a TreePPL MCMC run

Source: R/post-process.R
tp_parse_mcmc.Rd

tp_parse_mcmc() reads the JSON output of a TreePPL run with a Markov chain Monte Carlo method (e.g. "mcmc", "mcmc-naive") and returns the samples as a tidy data frame (tibble), with one row per iteration.

Usage

tp_parse_mcmc(json_path, wide = TRUE)

Arguments

json_path

Path(s) to one or more JSON output files, as returned by tp_run(). Each file is one run.

wide

Logical. If TRUE (default), one row per iteration and one column per parameter. If FALSE, one row per iteration and parameter, with columns parameter and sample.

Value

A tibble (tidy data frame) with columns:

  • run: run number, in the order of json_path.

  • iteration: iteration number within its run.

  • one column per parameter (wide = TRUE), or parameter and sample (wide = FALSE).

Details

Both TreePPL output formats are read, and the format is detected automatically:

  • by default, the file holds one line with all samples ({"samples": [...], "weights": [...], "normConst": ...});

  • with incremental printing (incremental_printing = TRUE in tp_sampler()), each sample is on its own line, followed by an empty summary line, which is ignored.

TreePPL writes NaN and infinite values as {"__float__": "nan"}; these are read as R's NaN, Inf and -Inf. MCMC weights are all equal, so they are not returned.

Parameters are named after the fields of the model's return type when the output has them (e.g. lambda, mu), and x1, x2, ... otherwise. Non-scalar values (vectors, trees) are kept as list-columns.

Files without samples are skipped with a warning. If no file has samples, the function stops with an error.

See also

tp_run(), which calls this function for MCMC runs, and tp_parse_smc() for SMC output.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sampler <- tp_sampler(model = "crbd", method = "mcmc")
run <- tp_run(sampler, data, iterations = 1000, n_runs = 2)

# Parse output files directly
samples <- tp_parse_mcmc(c("out1.json", "out2.json"))
samples_long <- tp_parse_mcmc("out1.json", wide = FALSE)

# Incremental printing gives the same result
sampler <- tp_sampler(model = "crbd", method = "mcmc", incremental_printing = TRUE)
run <- tp_run(sampler, data, iterations = 1000)
} # }
